IEE Colloquium on Transport Telematics in the Fourth Framework (Digest No: 1996/070)
abstract: EUROSCOPE builds upon the results and infrastructure produced within the DRIVE II project SCOPE to demonstrate a number of integrated Advanced Transport Telematic (ATT) applications. Within the United Kingdom, this will be achieved through the continuation and expansion of the ROMANSE project in Southampton and South Hampshire. EUROSCOPE (Efficient Urban tRansport Operations Services and Cooperation Of Ports cities in Europe) has "port cities" as the common theme. It has expanded the original SCOPE consortium of Cologne, Hampshire, and Piraeus, within the European Union fourth framework programme, to include Rotterdam, Strasbourg, Genoa, Hamburg, as new "core" partners with Cork, and Brandenburg, as followers, each region having a major port facility. The emphasis of the project is on the provision of large scale demonstrators which have a direct application for the cities, port or operator and which, in turn, will be inter-operable throughout Europe. The EUROSCOPE consortium includes regional authorities, public transport operators, port and transhipment centres, industrial system providers, broadcasters, transport consultancies and research specialists.

articleTitle: The DIATS project: deployment of inter-urban ATT test scenarios
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transport Telematics in the Fourth Framework (Digest No: 1996/070)
abstract: Describes the DIATS project which is concerned with the development of scenarios describing the deployment of interurban and periurban ATT measures based on co-operative driving concepts, DGVII Task 7.3/20. The main output of the project will be an assessment of these scenarios (including an indication of the robustness of the likely forecasts), in terms of both content and timing, with key alternatives and issues being identified, and their implications considered. To achieve this output, research activities will address three interim goals that divide the project into its main functional stages.

articleTitle: INCOME: integration of traffic control with other measures
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transport Telematics in the Fourth Framework (Digest No: 1996/070)
abstract: INCOME is a new "Fourth Framework" collaborative project sponsored by DGVII (Transport) of the European Commission (EC) in the domain of Urban Transport. The 3 year project started in January 1996 and is targeting the task specified in the DGVII workplan as "Strategies for Optimising Multi-faceted Systems" and is centred on Integrated Urban Traffic Management systems (UTMS) which are being developed in many European cities on the platforms provided by Advanced Urban Traffic Control (UTC). The project involves eight partners from five European cities. The partners are listed together with the cities where the INCOME strategies will be evaluated.

articleTitle: Management of traffic using control and other measures: MUSIC
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transport Telematics in the Fourth Framework (Digest No: 1996/070)
abstract: For many years traffic signals in urban areas have been used to control road networks, primarily to minimise the total delay to vehicles. Traffic patterns have generally been assumed to be fixed and little or no account has been taken of route choice. In recent years, local bus priority measures have been introduced which also supposed that the traffic patterns were fixed and also did not take account of route choice. More recently gating strategies have been introduced to protect more sensitive areas by controlling traffic patterns but again the effects of rerouting have not been taken into account. The aim of the MUSIC project is to demonstrate that by managing and optimising the overall performance of the network using new, cost effective, traffic control strategies it will be possible to: reduce congestion; improve the efficiency of public transport; and influence mode choice. This will be achieved by using the MUSIC software package which calculates area-wide traffic signal timings.

articleTitle: MATTISSE paints the future for travellers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transport Telematics in the Fourth Framework (Digest No: 1996/070)
abstract: The MATTISSE project as currently defined, represents an ambitious but achievable demonstration of Advanced Transport Telematics for the Midlands Region. Building as it does on the pilot trials of QUARTET a most important feature is that it utilises the existing infrastructure of control systems within each partners area. It will provide for the comprehensive exchange of information and development of control strategies to the benefit of both network managers and transport users alike. MATTISSE paints the future for travellers.

articleTitle: The demonstration and development of SOCRATES in the Fourth Framework programme
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transport Telematics in the Fourth Framework (Digest No: 1996/070)
abstract: SOCRATES stands for "system of cellular radio for travel efficiency and safety". SOCRATES 3 is a major demonstration project in the Transport Telematics application area of the Fourth Framework programme of research and technological development. The basis for the project is the demonstration of SOCRATES services in three European sites: Hessen and North Rhine Westfalen in Germany and the EuroDelta test site in the Netherlands. The objectives of the project are to: conduct a validation and demonstration of interoperable transport telematics services based on SOCRATES; demonstrate international interoperability of SOCRATES services; provide support for the commercial introduction of SOCRATES services; continue the evaluation and demonstration of SOCRATES services based on an upgraded system; establish and develop administrative and organisational links (public-private partnership); further develop the SOCRATES systems architecture, protocol and geographic database standardisation; conduct a design study for SOCRATES implementation in Barcelona; and contribute to European standardisation activities for transport telematics.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transport Telematics in the Fourth Framework (Digest No: 1996/070)
abstract: The TABASCO (Telematics Applications in BAvaria, SCotland and Others) project is a European demonstration project implementing multi-modal information and control systems as a contribution towards solving transport problems of cities in regions. The first part of the paper provides a general overview of the project, describing the project objectives, application areas and demonstration sites. The second part focuses on one of the main application areas: inter-urban or regional network control and information.

articleTitle: ELGAR: an experiment in air quality information display and its impact on driver behaviour
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transport Telematics in the Fourth Framework (Digest No: 1996/070)
abstract: Describes the ELGAR (Environment Led Guidance and Restraint) project is designed to assess the impact on traveller behaviour of a number of measures to advise travellers of air quality in Bristol city centre and encourage use of an existing Park and Ride service. ELGAR combines the use of existing traffic control measures, e.g. UTC, and future measures, e.g. variable message signs and bus automatic vehicle location. ELGAR will connect these systems together and control the information flow between the systems for maximum effectiveness. Operating fully automatically, ELGAR will not require dedicated operators.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transport Telematics in the Fourth Framework (Digest No: 1996/070)
abstract: This paper describes the objectives and work so far undertaken in the VADE MECUM EC Fourth Framework Transport Telematics Design Study. VADE MECUM is a one year project involving a consortium of 26 partners along a "corridor site" wrapped around parts of the TransEuropean Road Network in Ireland (North and South), across North Wales, North West England, Yorkshire and Humberside, through the Humber ports and on to the Netherlands. It is co-funded by the European Commission Directorate General XIII to the value of 500,000 ECU. The acronym VADE MECUM stands for Vehicle ATT Demonstrations, Evaluation and monitoring on a European Corridor Uniting Member states.

articleTitle: Transport telematics project TR1002: ADEPT II (Automatic Debiting and Electronic Payment for Transport II)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Transport Telematics in the Fourth Framework (Digest No: 1996/070)
abstract: The 4th Framework Programme's ADEPT II project builds upon on the work of the earlier EU's (3rd Framework Programme) DRIVE Project ADEPT which addressed the design and evaluation of demand management schemes resulting from the technical development and deployment of transponders and smart-card based payment systems for road transport. ADEPT itself was regarded as a highly successful and innovative project which had six highly successful trial sites covering non-stop multi-lane tolling, road-use pricing (congestion pricing), car park management, booking and debiting and in all trials additional driver information and payment services using the same telematics equipment. In order to clearly understand the context of ADEPT II a description of some of the main achievements of the ADEPT project is given.
